facts.summary: Utah's minimum wage is $7.25 per hour, the same as the federal minimum wage.
facts.citation: Utah Code Ann. Sec. 34-40-101 et seq. (Utah Minimum Wage Act)
facts.sourceAgency: Utah Labor Commission, Antidiscrimination and Labor Division (UALD)
facts.notes: Utah adopts the federal rate and has not enacted a higher state minimum. Verify the current-year figure against the Labor Commission page.

facts.summary: Tipped employees may be paid $2.13 per hour so long as tips plus the base wage total at least $7.25 per hour.
facts.citation: Utah Code Ann. Sec. 34-40-101 et seq. (Utah Minimum Wage Act)
facts.sourceAgency: Utah Labor Commission, Antidiscrimination and Labor Division (UALD)
facts.notes: Mirrors the federal tip-credit floor. Applies to adults and minors.

facts.summary: Minors under 18 may be paid a training wage of $4.25 per hour during their first 90 days of employment.
facts.citation: Utah Code Ann. Sec. 34-40-101 et seq. (Utah Minimum Wage Act)
facts.sourceAgency: Utah Labor Commission, Antidiscrimination and Labor Division (UALD)
facts.notes: Mirrors the federal youth-training wage; applies only to the first 90 consecutive calendar days.

facts.summary: Utah has no separate state overtime law; overtime is governed by the federal FLSA (time-and-a-half after 40 hours per week, no daily overtime).
facts.citation: Utah Code Ann. Sec. 34-40-101 et seq. (Utah Minimum Wage Act)
facts.sourceAgency: Utah Labor Commission, Antidiscrimination and Labor Division (UALD)
facts.notes: Utah's Minimum Wage Act does not impose a daily-overtime or higher salary threshold beyond federal law. Inferred from absence of a state overtime provision; confirm no separate rule applies to a specific industry.

facts.summary: Beyond the federal protected classes, Utah's Antidiscrimination Act also prohibits employment discrimination based on sexual orientation, gender identity, and pregnancy/childbirth-related conditions.
facts.citation: Utah Code Ann. Sec. 34A-5-101 et seq. (Utah Antidiscrimination Act)
facts.sourceAgency: Utah Labor Commission, Antidiscrimination and Labor Division (UALD)
facts.notes: Full Utah list also includes race, color, religion, sex, age (40+), national origin, and disability, which overlap with federal law. Sexual orientation and gender identity were added by 2015 legislation.

facts.summary: The Utah Antidiscrimination Act applies to employers with 15 or more employees, the same threshold as Title VII.
facts.citation: Utah Code Ann. Sec. 34A-5-102 (Utah Antidiscrimination Act)
facts.sourceAgency: Utah Labor Commission, Antidiscrimination and Labor Division (UALD)
facts.notes: Same as federal 15-employee threshold; not lower. Certain national-origin, citizenship, or equal-pay matters may have lower thresholds.

facts.summary: A discrimination charge must be filed with UALD within 180 days of the last alleged discriminatory act.
facts.citation: Utah Code Ann. Sec. 34A-5-107 (Utah Antidiscrimination Act)
facts.sourceAgency: Utah Labor Commission, Antidiscrimination and Labor Division (UALD)
facts.notes: Shorter than the federal 300-day deadline. Charges filed between 180 and 300 days are forwarded to the EEOC rather than processed by UALD.

facts.value: involuntary: within 24 hours of separation; voluntary: next regular payday
facts.summary: An employee who is fired or laid off must be paid all wages within 24 hours of separation; an employee who resigns is paid on the next regular payday.
facts.citation: Utah Code Ann. Sec. 34-28-5 (Utah Payment of Wages Act)
facts.sourceAgency: Utah Labor Commission, Antidiscrimination and Labor Division (UALD)
facts.notes: State of Utah government employees are exempted from the 24-hour rule. This is a state-specific requirement with no direct federal equivalent.
